section_summary: This section continues a classified interrogation report on Japanese wartime intelligence operations in Europe, first discussing deception material received by Onodera and then detailing Japanese cooperation with Polish, Finnish, Baltic, German, Hungarian, and Swedish intelligence personnel. It describes agent networks against the Soviet Union, exchanges of military and political intelligence, Finnish cryptanalytic cooperation, German Abwehr contacts, and liaison among Japanese military missions. The final pages begin a source-by-source table summarizing the intelligence supplied and its targets.

subfiles.title: Japanese wartime intelligence in Europe: contacts, sources, and intelligence obtained
subfiles.about: Continuation of a report reconstructing the European intelligence contacts, cooperative arrangements, agent networks, and information sources of Japanese military attachés Onodera and Onouchi.
subfiles.summary: The report first records deceptive Allied and German information passed to Onodera, then describes the historical and wartime development of Japanese cooperation with Polish, Finnish, Estonian, Latvian, German, Hungarian, and Swedish intelligence personnel. It gives detailed accounts of Rybikowski's Polish network, Finnish cryptanalytic stations and refugee organization, Baltic agent systems inside the Soviet Union, and Onodera's contacts with the Abwehr and other military attachés. It also surveys exchanges among Japanese missions in Berlin, Helsinki, Madrid, Lisbon, Ankara, and elsewhere. Pages 74-77 begin a tabular summary identifying sources, subsources, intelligence supplied, and target countries.
